manifest.name: alert-dialog
manifest.title: AlertDialog
manifest.description: A decision the user must make before going on, on Base UI's AlertDialog: Dialog's scrim and popup with role="alertdialog", no close button and no dismissal by an outside click, a Cancel and an Action in the footer.
manifest.usage: Use AlertDialog to confirm an action that destroys data or cannot be undone (delete a connection, run a destructive statement) or to approve something with consequences (grant access). Compose it as AlertDialog > AlertDialogTrigger (render a Button; or open it through open) + AlertDialogContent > AlertDialogHeader (AlertDialogTitle: the question or consequence; AlertDialogDescription), an optional AlertDialogBody (the statement, the target), AlertDialogFooter (AlertDialogCancel, then the action). An action that finishes at once can be an AlertDialogCancel with variant="danger" (it closes); an action that waits for the core is an AlertDialogAction with loading, and the caller closes the dialog through open when it succeeds. Name the action after what it does ("Delete", "Approve and save"), not "OK". For a task that may be dismissed freely use Dialog.

props.name: size
props.description: The popup's maximum width, from size.panel.*, as Dialog's.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state; defaultOpen when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the trigger, an AlertDialogCancel or Escape opens or closes it.

props.name: variant
props.description: AlertDialogAction (default primary) and AlertDialogCancel (default ghost): the Button's variant.

props.name: loading
props.description: AlertDialogAction: the action is running; the Button ignores clicks and sets aria-busy.

props.name: initialFocus
props.description: AlertDialogContent: the element focused on open (default: the first focusable, usually Cancel).

props.name: className
props.description: On each part: extra classes, merged after the component's own.

slots.name: backdrop
slots.description: The scrim, color.bg.scrim at z.overlay; data-slot="alert-dialog-backdrop".

slots.name: viewport
slots.description: The fixed centring layer at z.modal with the region's data-theme and data-density; data-slot="alert-dialog-viewport".

slots.name: popup
slots.description: role="alertdialog", color.bg.overlay with elevation.modal; data-slot="alert-dialog-content", data-size.

parts.name: AlertDialogTrigger
parts.description: Opens the dialog; unstyled, render a Button through render.

parts.name: AlertDialogContent
parts.description: The portal with the scrim, the viewport and the popup; no close button.

parts.name: AlertDialogViewport
parts.description: The centring layer; AlertDialogContent renders it.

parts.name: AlertDialogTitle
parts.description: An <h2> in type.heading-4 that names the dialog.

parts.name: AlertDialogDescription
parts.description:
A

in color.fg.muted that describes the dialog.

parts.name: AlertDialogBody
parts.description: What the decision is about; scrolls when long.

parts.name: AlertDialogFooter
parts.description: Cancel, then the action, at the end of the row.

parts.name: AlertDialogCancel
parts.description: A Button (ghost by default) that closes the dialog.

parts.name: AlertDialogAction
parts.description: A Button (primary by default) that runs the action and does not close the dialog by itself.

states.name: open
states.description: Opening: Dialog's scale and fade over motion.duration.slow; reduced motion turns them off.

states.name: loading
states.description: AlertDialogAction with loading: the Button ignores clicks while the action runs.

accessibility: The popup is role="alertdialog", named by AlertDialogTitle and described by AlertDialogDescription; while it is open the rest of the page is inert and hidden from assistive technology.
Opening moves focus to the first focusable element (Cancel in the usual footer order, so Enter does not confirm by accident); Tab stays inside; closing returns focus to the trigger.
Escape closes it (as Cancel); a press outside does not.
The action names what it does; a destructive one uses the danger variant and its text, so the meaning does not rest on colour.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the scale and fade transitions off.
